svg.title: Inside QueryAtlas: one question travelling through the machine
svg.desc: A question typed in a chat terminal becomes a glowing packet that passes through QueryAtlas's engine: access check, database router, knowledge vault (40 tables narrowed to 2), query writer, validator seal with the tenant filter attached, encrypted tunnel to the database with a countdown, rows returning as a table and chart, then a verified example flowing back into the vault. The audit tape records each step.
svg.text: one question, travelling through the machine

g.text: MCP over stdio / HTTP+OAuth · web: POST /api/query/stream
✓ session token valid · expires in 12 h
3 open · this chat is bound to
switching to another open database: instant, no reconnect
customers ⟷ orders (join confirmed by the data)
+ glossary note, value hints, a verified example
~600 tokens of context instead of the whole schema

text.tspan: orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id=o.customer_id
c.name ORDER BY spent DESC LIMIT 5

g.text: A: QueryAtlas's AI (Groq · OpenAI · Ollama) or B: Claude writes it
time limit, enforced by the database
database.fetch_read · row cap · one repair round if it errors
“Acme Retail spent the most last month —
cached per question & tenant · streamed in the web app
question → query stored (without the tenant value)
shown first next time · wrong ones deleted
Ann types a question. It can arrive from Claude Code, Cursor or the web app.
The engine checks who she is, what her role allows, and that she is within limits.
Several databases are open for her; this chat is bound to Sales on PostgreSQL.
The vault is scanned: 40 tables shrink to 2, with a data-confirmed join, her team's notes and value hints.
The SQL is written — by QueryAtlas's own AI, or by Claude itself.
The validator seals it: read-only, no credential columns, tenant filter attached, caps set.
It runs through an encrypted tunnel with a time limit the database enforces. Rows come back.
The answer: a table, a chart and one sentence — and a line on the audit tape.
Ann confirms it. The verified example flows back into the vault, ready for next time.
